PullRequest.Title: Experimental Fusion model picker with inline tier presentation
PullRequest.Body:
This pull request introduces a new presentation for the Fusion model tiers in the model picker, which is enabled by a hidden setting. Key changes include:

- **Inline Presentation**: Fusion tiers are now displayed as taller inline entries labeled **Standard**, **High**, and **Max**.
- **Single Button Display**: The model picker button shows **Fusion <Tier>** without a separate effort level button.
- **Alignment Fixes**: Checkmarks are aligned in the left-hand column, and the line height for the "High" label has been adjusted to prevent clipping.
- **Testing and Verification**: All changes have been verified with 367 passing tests, and regression checks have been added to ensure stability.

The new feature maintains existing functionality for keyboard navigation and search, while providing a visually distinct presentation for Fusion models.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed action is explicitly async and awaits setModelConfigValues, and the changed delegate explicitly waits for thenables before hide(). The traced implementation synchronously writes the chat-scoped storage bucket, then awaits ILanguageModelsService.setModelConfiguration, which reads/parses and saves the language-models profile file and reads/parses it again. The only uncertainty is the absolute duration on a given filesystem, not the mechanism or critical-path reachability.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Scoped storage writes plus language-model profile filesystem reads, JSON parsing, and save operations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each distinct tier click queues another per-model configuration edit; latency grows with filesystem delay, language-model configuration file size, and additional clicks made while the popup remains open.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Blocked interaction critical path and increased tier-selection latency
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this diff, selecting a model row applied the selection and hid the picker synchronously; configuration edits were available only in the details flow, where keeping the details open was intentional. No direct picker-close path waited for profile persistence.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Selecting a mutable inline Fusion tier now keeps the model picker open and delays applying the model until configuration persistence has fully completed.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added inline-tier action at RIGHT line 1152 awaits setModelConfigValues before applying the model selection; the same diff changes the selection delegate at lines 530-537 to defer hide() until that returned promise resolves.
Findings.Title: Do not block tier selection on profile-file persistence
Findings.Impact: With inline tiers enabled, clicking Standard/High/Max can leave the popup visibly open and the requested model unapplied for the duration of profile-file I/O. On a slow or busy profile filesystem, this makes a basic picker selection feel stuck; repeated clicks while it remains open can also queue additional serialized saves.
Findings.Evidence: setModelConfigValues queues per model and awaits configurationAccess.setModelConfiguration. In normal chat, ChatModelConfigurationStore.setModelConfiguration first persists the scoped bucket, then awaits ILanguageModelsService.setModelConfiguration. That service updates the language-models configuration through LanguageModelsConfigurationService, whose update path performs fileService.exists, creates/parses a text-model reference, saves the profile file, and reloads/parses it. The new delegate does not hide the picker until this chain settles.
Findings.Recommendation: Hide the picker immediately after accepting the inline tier and keep only selection ordering/cancellation behind the save promise, or update the scoped in-memory value/apply the selection synchronously and persist in the background with explicit error reporting. Do not make popup dismissal await the profile-file write.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or search the tabbed model picker with inline Fusion tiers enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening builds destinations, sections, the Fusion header, and the effective tier rows synchronously before the popup is usable. Typing filters the in-memory action list. The added tier count is small and does not put an expensive boundary on this path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Available models/providers plus the provider's Fusion tier enum; typically a few tiers and tens of models, with only visible rows rendered.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI-thread list construction/render and filtering; no asynchronous fan-out, limiter, or queue is reached.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Model metadata and effective configuration are read from in-memory service maps after the chat-scoped configuration store's first read. The action list is virtualized; search filtering reuses the built item set rather than fetching remote data. No negative cache is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the open/search call flow and in-memory construction are explicit in createActionList, _buildFusionItems, and ActionListWidget.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The total model count varies by installed providers, but the diff adds only the small provider tier enum and existing list virtualization bounds rendered DOM rows.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds bounded tier-row construction and small string/DOM allocations, while retaining virtualization and in-memory filtering.

Scenarios.Scenario: Select Standard, High, or Max from the inline Fusion tier rows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The added row action awaits setModelConfigValues; the changed selection delegate waits for the action promise before hide(). Therefore scoped persistence and profile-file operations must complete before model selection and popup dismissal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist a tier to chat-scoped storage and rewrite/reload the language-model profile JSON file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One scoped StorageService write for a changed value, followed normally by one global model-configuration update. That update performs one profile-file update cycle (exists/read+parse/save) and one reload cycle (exists/read+parse); multiple configuration-only groups can multiply update cycles.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Plain model selection applied and hid synchronously. The same persistence boundary existed for edits in the model details page, but it was not newly placed on a direct picker-dismissal path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All operations are awaited by the new inline action, and the popup hide callback waits for the action promise, so they directly delay visible interaction completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Filesystem latency and configuration JSON size; additional distinct clicks made while the popup remains open add serialized persistence cycles.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: SequencerByKey serializes edits per model. Rapid clicks do not run filesystem writes concurrently, but distinct tier changes queue and extend total latency; there is no latest-value coalescing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The chat-scoped configuration is cached in memory, but a real changed tier is persisted to both the scoped storage bucket and profile-global language-model configuration. A repeated identical value can become a no-op after an earlier edit completes, but distinct queued values are not coalesced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: both awaits, the per-model sequencer, scoped storage write, and profile file read/save/re-read implementation are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Absolute delay depends on profile file size, platform storage, filesystem load, and whether multiple configuration groups exist. The hidden setting limits prevalence, which lowers severity but not confidence in the latency mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity latency regression: the new direct selection path blocks model application and popup dismissal on persistence I/O.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render the chat input model label as Fusion Standard/High/Max
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration/model events call _renderLabel synchronously. The diff adds tier-label derivation and suppresses a separate configuration button, but no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network call is reached by the added label logic.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing model count for routing lookup and the frequency of model/configuration events; no lifetime-retained collection is added.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI-thread render update; event delivery is synchronous and no queue or fan-out was added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: getModelConfigProperty reads the effective configuration from the chat-scoped in-memory map after initialization or from the language-model service's in-memory map. Routing scans reuse the already supplied model array.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed _renderLabel code and configuration access implementations show in-memory reads on this path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Render frequency follows existing entitlement, model, and configuration events; model arrays vary in size, but the added work is constant-time configuration lookup plus existing linear routing searches.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added work is bounded string/configuration lookup and does not introduce an expensive boundary or meaningful retained state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render separators with optional detail text in action lists
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Visible list-row rendering creates/updates the detail span and writes its text/display state. Geometry is not synchronously read after these writes in production code, and row height is computed from item metadata.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of simultaneously realized separator rows, not total historical list items or application lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI-thread rendering of only realized rows; no asynchronous work or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Separator templates are recycled by the virtualized action list. Each realized separator now owns one additional detail span; element disposables are cleared on reuse.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: SeparatorRenderer and ActionListWidget height calculation directly show allocation and reuse behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of visible separators varies by action-list consumer, but virtualization bounds realized templates and the added node is one per realized separator.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The extra recycled span and style/text updates are bounded and do not establish layout thrashing, unbounded retention, or dropped-frame risk.

Scenarios.Scenario: Enable or disable the inline Fusion presentation setting
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Changing the hidden inline-tier setting triggers one label render and, if the picker exists, one refresh/rebuild. This is user/configuration-event driven rather than per-frame or per-keystroke.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Frequency of changes to the single hidden setting and current model-list size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous event listeners; one refresh per configuration event with no subprocess or remote operation introduced by the changed listeners.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The setting value is served by IConfigurationService; picker context and model metadata are already resident. Rebuilding uses the same list/widget lifecycle and does not add a cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the two changed affectsConfiguration branches directly call _renderLabel or refresh.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Configuration changes are infrequent; extension or sync-driven churn is possible but no evidence shows realistic high-frequency updates.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. A one-time picker rebuild and label render are proportional to the existing model list and occur on an infrequent setting event.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 13 changed files and paginated diffs. One diff-introduced critical-path I/O regression was reported: inline tier selection awaits scoped/profile persistence before applying the model and dismissing the picker. Opening/searching, label rendering, setting refresh, accessibility composition, and generic separator rendering remain bounded and introduce no reportable expensive boundary or retention mechanism.
